text.p: Following are some of the
main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified
these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Opposition Christian Democrats and coalition Liberals
call for cuts in wealth tax. (p1)
- Senior staff member at food and drinks group BolsWessanen
arrested on suspicion of insider trading. (p1)
- Van Lanschot Bankiers forecasts 12-20 percent profit
growth compared with 1995, which was a good year too. (p1)
- Brewer Grolsch books first half net up 11 pct despite
lower margins. (p3)
- Computer systems firm Multihouse boosts net profit to
114,000 guilders from 91,000 guilders on higher turnover. (p3)
- Cable maker Draka books 22 pct higher H1 net, company
forecasts strong growth of full year result. (p3)
- Businesses in the Amsterdam area expect higher 1996
results. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch carrier KLM cuts rates up to 40 pct on a number of
European flights as airlines price war hots up. (p2)
- Dutch natural gas supplier Gasunie loses industrial
customers to Energie Zuid Nederland EZN, which supplies gas from
England. (p3)
- Property company Capa City Realty buys real estate worth
83 million guilders. (p23)
- Companies with sound anti-takeover constructions perform
better, according to research by securities house Effectenbank
Stroeve. (p23)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Russia's aircraft makers Yakovlev and Tupolev rekindle
interest in taking over planemaker Fokker. (p1)
- Sharp profit growth for retail and services group
Goudsmit. (p33)
- Philips Electronics to sell its television production
plant in Tennessee, U.S. (p33)
- Chemicals giant Akzo Nobel signs letter of intent
with Chinese firm to build new industrial fibre plant in
China for an initial investment of 125 million guilders. (p35)
TROUW
- Queen Beatrix opens the Erasmus bridge, also called the
Swan, that links Rotterdam Port across the Maas river. (p1)
- Technical wholesaler Reesink forcasts slightly lower full
year results. (p24)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Sweets producer Van Melle lifts first six months net to
Dfl 24.1 mln from Dfl 22.3 mln in the year-earlier half. (p10)
- Telecom giant Global One seeks to compete with Dutch PTT
in telephone service lines. (p11)
